note: Hand-authored things to find, laid over the map. Keep these few: the game is about wandering the town, not about reaching rings. Each is placed by naming a map feature (near), a street bridge (bridge), the longest trail footbridge (trailBridge), or a fraction along the longest open creek or trail piece (creek, trail). kind is 'story' (a history moment), 'wear' (something for the cat to wear; item names the piece) or 'skill' (an extra trick; item names it).

spots.title: Main Street Bridge
spots.blurb: Today's bridge crosses the freeway. Until the 1950s, an arched bridge of 1906 crossed the creek here.

spots.title: The Mill Annex
spots.blurb: This stone store-room of 1880 is all that remains of the four-storey flour mill James Alexander Forbes built in the 1850s.

spots.title: The High School
spots.blurb: The main building was dedicated in 1925, designed by W. H. Weeks, on its rise of lawn above Main Street.

spots.title: Town Plaza
spots.blurb: Under the old cedar, you find your voice. Tap Meow and people nearby stop to say hello.

spots.title: A beret
spots.blurb: Left on the kerb outside the theatre. It fits rather well.

spots.title: Reading glasses
spots.blurb: Someone's spare pair, by the library steps. Very distinguished.

spots.title: A daisy chain
spots.blurb: Woven by somebody on the creek bank and left for whoever came by.
